english: Even I need to relax at the end of the day. Helps keep me sharp.
french: Moi aussi, j'ai besoin de me détendre en fin de journée. Ça me permet de rester en forme le reste du temps.
russian: Даже мне нужно расслабляться в конце дня. Это помогает оставаться собранной.
bulgarian: Even I need to relax at the end of the day. Helps keep me sharp.

english: Adeline and I don't talk much on our work dates, but it's just nice to have the company. And I can occasionally offer her some advice... there's a lot on that young lady's shoulders.
french: Adeline et moi ne nous parlons pas beaucoup lors de nos séances de travail, mais j'aime sa compagnie. Et il m’arrive de lui donner des conseils... Elle a tant de responsabilités.
russian: Мы с Аделиной не особо болтаем во время наших рабочих встреч, но просто приятно, когда рядом кто-то есть. Иногда могу дать ей совет... у этой девушки многое на плечах.
bulgarian: Adeline and I don't talk much on our work dates, but it's just nice to have the company. And I can occasionally offer her some advice... there's a lot on that young lady's shoulders.

english: Adeline's got big plans for rebuilding Mistria, and we can all be a part of it. Especially you, [Ari].
french: Adeline a de grands projets pour la redynamisation de Mistria et nous avons tous notre rôle à jouer. Ça vaut particulièrement pour toi, [Ari].
russian: У Аделины большие планы по восстановлению Мистрии, и мы все можем стать их частью. Особенно ты, [Ari].
bulgarian: Adeline's got big plans for rebuilding Mistria, and we can all be a part of it. Especially you, [Ari].

english: I know Dell, I know... they're not sandwiches, they're "adventuring rations".
french: Je sais, Dell, je sais... Ce ne sont pas de simples sandwichs... Ce sont des « rations d'aventuriers ».
russian: Знаю, Делл, знаю... это не сэндвичи, это «походные пайки».
bulgarian: I know Dell, I know... they're not sandwiches, they're "adventuring rations".

english: Best not to wait on balancing the books.
french: Mieux vaut ne pas perdre de temps pour la compta.
russian: Не стоит откладывать учёт.
bulgarian: Best not to wait on balancing the books.

english: Good to see you, [Ari].
french: Quel plaisir de te voir, [Ari].
russian: Рада тебя видеть, [Ari].
bulgarian: Good to see you, [Ari].

english: It's just so relaxing!
french: C'est le meilleur moyen de se détendre !
russian: Она просто очень расслабляет!
bulgarian: It's just so relaxing!

english: I'm so happy Juniper opened up her bathhouse. I could say it's because it makes Mistria more attractive to visitors, but honestly?
french: Je suis contente que Juniper ait rouvert les bains. Je pourrais prétendre que c'est parce que ça attire plus de touristes à Mistria, mais tu veux connaître la vraie raison ?
russian: Я так рада, что Джунипер открыла купальню. Могла бы сказать, что это хорошо для туризма, но по правде?
bulgarian: I'm so happy Juniper opened up her bathhouse. I could say it's because it makes Mistria more attractive to visitors, but honestly?

english: My back was so cramped after a day hunched over the accounting... thank goodness Juniper opened up the Bathhouse.
french: J'avais mal au dos après une journée passée à faire ma comptabilité... Je ne remercierai jamais assez Juniper d'avoir rouvert les bains.
russian: У меня так спина затекла после дня за бухгалтерией... хорошо, что теперь у нас есть купальня.
bulgarian: My back was so cramped after a day hunched over the accounting... thank goodness Juniper opened up the Bathhouse.

english: I appreciate everything you've done for the town, [Ari]! It's been such a boon to have a farmer just down the road.
french: Je tiens à te remercier pour tout ce que tu fais pour la ville, [Ari] ! Quelle aubaine d'avoir <she>une agricultrice</she><he>un agriculteur</he><they>un·e agriculteur·rice</they> juste à côté.
russian:
Спасибо за всё, что ты

сделали

сделаласделалсделало для города, [Ari]! Так здорово, что твоя ферма рядом.
bulgarian: I appreciate everything you've done for the town, [Ari]! It's been such a boon to have a farmer just down the road.

english: I know better than to balance the books before I've eaten.
french: Je ne me mets jamais à la comptabilité le ventre vide.
russian: Я знаю, что не стоит браться за учёт на голодный желудок.
bulgarian: I know better than to balance the books before I've eaten.

english: It's been busy today! I guess everyone's getting ready for Inn night.
french: Je n'ai pas arrêté aujourd'hui ! J'imagine que tout le monde se prépare à se rendre à l'auberge.
russian: Сегодня было оживлённо! Видимо, все готовятся к вечеру в трактире.
bulgarian: It's been busy today! I guess everyone's getting ready for Inn night.

english: She does a little work at the store and then grows flowers and herbs on the side... But can she really make a living doing that?
french: Elle travaille un peu au magasin et cultive aussi des fleurs et des plantes, à côté de ça, mais... est-ce qu'elle arrive à gagner sa vie ?
russian: Немного подрабатывает в магазине, а на стороне выращивает цветы и травы... Но разве этим можно прожить?
bulgarian: She does a little work at the store and then grows flowers and herbs on the side... But can she really make a living doing that?

english: If she spent less time with her nose in the $Codex Mistria$, she might apply herself more.
french: Si elle passait moins de temps le nez plongé dans le $Codex Mistria$, elle pourrait se consacrer davantage à son activité.
russian: Если бы она поменьше сидела, уткнувшись в $«Кодекс Мистрии»$, то, может, взялась бы за ум.
bulgarian: If she spent less time with her nose in the $Codex Mistria$, she might apply herself more.

english: Sigh...
french: Soupir...
russian: Эх...
bulgarian: Sigh...

english: I hope Celine is getting along alright.
french: J'espère que Céline s'en sort.
russian: Надеюсь, у Селин всё в порядке.
bulgarian: I hope Celine is getting along alright.

english: Sounds like there's going to be a bit of a crowd at the Inn tonight, [Ari]. Hope to see you there!
french: Apparemment, il y aura du monde à l'auberge ce soir, [Ari]. J'espère que tu seras des nôtres !
russian: Похоже, в трактире сегодня будет людно, [Ari]. Надеюсь, увидимся там!
bulgarian: Sounds like there's going to be a bit of a crowd at the Inn tonight, [Ari]. Hope to see you there!

english: No more climbing them.
french: Tu n'escalades pas.
russian: Хватит по ним лазать.
bulgarian: No more climbing them.

english: Dell, if you can't reach a shelf just ask me, okay?
french: Dell, si tu n'arrives pas à atteindre une étagère, tu me demandes, entendu ?
russian: Делл, если не дотягиваешься до полки — просто скажи мне, ладно?
bulgarian: Dell, if you can't reach a shelf just ask me, okay?

english: Dell was awake when I got up... she wasn't up all night, was she?
french: Dell était déjà réveillée quand je me suis levée... J'espère qu'elle n'est pas restée debout toute la nuit.
russian: Когда я проснулась, Делл уже не спала... Она же не всю ночь бодрствовала?
bulgarian: Dell was awake when I got up... she wasn't up all night, was she?

english: I don't know what Holt's worried about, Dell's a heavy sleeper. She always sleeps through when it's time to stock the shelves in the morning.
french: Je ne sais pas pourquoi Holt s'inquiète, Dell est une grosse dormeuse. Elle ne se réveille même pas le matin, quand on réapprovisionne les rayons.
russian: Не знаю, чего Хольт беспокоится: Делл спит как убитая. Даже когда надо раскладывать товар с утра.
bulgarian: I don't know what Holt's worried about, Dell's a heavy sleeper. She always sleeps through when it's time to stock the shelves in the morning.

english: A morning bath wakes me right up!
french: Un bon bain le matin me donne de l'énergie pour toute la journée !
russian: Утренняя ванна меня сразу бодрит!
bulgarian: A morning bath wakes me right up!

english: I'm so glad I got to sneak a bath in before my shift!
french: Je suis si contente d'avoir pu prendre un bain avant d'aller travailler !
russian: Так рада, что успела сбегать в купальню до начала смены!
bulgarian: I'm so glad I got to sneak a bath in before my shift!

english: We've got sugar, flour and rice... everything you need to jump into cooking!
french: Nous avons du sucre, de la farine, du riz... Tout ce qu'il faut pour se mettre aux fourneaux !
russian: У нас есть сахар, мука и рис... всё, чтобы сразу приступить к готовке!
bulgarian: We've got sugar, flour and rice... everything you need to jump into cooking!

english: I can't remember when my feet started aching after a long day at the shop. The years do catch up.
french: Ça fait déjà bien longtemps que j'ai mal aux pieds après une journée passée au magasin. C'est ça de vieillir.
russian: Не помню, когда ноги стали ныть после долгого дня в магазине. Годы берут своё.
bulgarian: I can't remember when my feet started aching after a long day at the shop. The years do catch up.

english: Welcome to Mistria. I'm Nora, I run the $General Store$ in town with my husband and our daughters.
french: Moi, c'est Nora. Je gère le $magasin général$ avec mon mari et nos filles.
russian: Я Нора. Мы с мужем и дочерьми управляем $универмагом$ в городе.
bulgarian: Welcome to Mistria. I'm Nora, I run the $General Store$ in town with my husband and our daughters.

english: I'm also head of the Chamber of Commerce and the $Saturday Market$...
french: Je suis aussi la présidente de la Chambre de commerce et je m'occupe du $marché du samedi$...
russian: Я также возглавляю Торговую палату и курирую $Субботний базар$...
bulgarian: I'm also head of the Chamber of Commerce and the $Saturday Market$...

english: Though unfortunately the $Saturday Market$ has been on hiatus since the earthquake caused the $bridge into town to collapse$.
french: Malheureusement, le tremblement de terre a causé l'$effondrement du pont$ et le $marché$ n'a pas pu reprendre.
russian: Хотя, к сожалению, $Субботний базар$ на паузе с тех пор, как землетрясение разрушило $мост в город$.
bulgarian: Though unfortunately the $Saturday Market$ has been on hiatus since the earthquake caused the $bridge into town to collapse$.

english: Balor is currently the only merchant that even attempts the trip these days. And he has to do it all on foot.
french: À l'heure actuelle, Balor est le seul marchand à faire le déplacement. Et à pied, en plus.
russian: Сейчас только Балор пытается добираться сюда, и то пешком.
bulgarian: Balor is currently the only merchant that even attempts the trip these days. And he has to do it all on foot.

english: Broken bridge? I think I can help!
french: Un pont qui s'est effondré ? Je dois pouvoir faire quelque chose !
russian: Сломанный мост? Думаю, я могу помочь!
bulgarian: Broken bridge? I think I can help!

english: What's the Saturday Market?
french: C'est quoi, le marché du samedi ?
russian: А что такое Субботний базар?
bulgarian: What's the Saturday Market?

english: Oh, right! Adeline did mention you'd be helping the town in exchange for the farm.
french: Mais oui ! Adeline a dit que tu aiderais notre petite ville en échange de la ferme.
russian:
Ах, да! Аделина говорила, что ты

будете помогать

будешь помогатьбудешь помогатьбудешь помогать городу в обмен на ферму.
bulgarian: Oh, right! Adeline did mention you'd be helping the town in exchange for the farm.

english: If the $broken bridge$ were repaired, all sorts of merchants could resume bringing their wares to town on Saturdays!
french: Si le $pont$ était remis en état, les marchands itinérants pourraient revenir vendre leurs produits ici, le samedi. Tu adorerais !
russian: Если $сломанный мост$ починить, торговцы снова смогут приезжать в город по субботам. Тебе точно понравится!
bulgarian: If the $broken bridge$ were repaired, all sorts of merchants could resume bringing their wares to town on Saturdays!

english: It used to be a weekly event in Mistria... All sorts of traveling merchants from around the Kingdom would stop here to sell their wares.
french: C'est un marché qui avait lieu une fois par semaine à Mistria... Des marchands itinérants de tout le royaume venaient ici vendre leurs produits.
russian: Раньше это было еженедельное событие в Мистрии... Торговцы со всего Королевства заезжали сюда продавать свои товары.
bulgarian: It used to be a weekly event in Mistria... All sorts of traveling merchants from around the Kingdom would stop here to sell their wares.

english: If the $broken bridge$ gets repaired, the $Saturday Market$ could resume!
french: Si le $pont$ était remis en état, le $marché du samedi$ pourrait reprendre. Tu adorerais !
russian: Если $сломанный мост$ восстановят, $Субботний базар$ снова заработает. Тебе точно понравится!
bulgarian: If the $broken bridge$ gets repaired, the $Saturday Market$ could resume!

english: Well, if you need anything in the way of seeds and supplies, please stop by the store.
french: Si tu as besoin de graines ou de provisions, n'hésite pas à passer nous voir au magasin.
russian: Как бы там ни было, если нужны семена или припасы — заходи в магазин в любое время.
bulgarian: Well, if you need anything in the way of seeds and supplies, please stop by the store.

english: Ah, you must be [Ari].
french: Ah, tu dois être [Ari] ! Bienvenue à Mistria.
russian: Ах, ты, должно быть, [Ari]! Добро пожаловать в Мистрию.
bulgarian: Ah, you must be [Ari].

english: Sales always go down during a heat wave.
french: On fait toujours moins de ventes quand il fait chaud.
russian: Во время жары продажи всегда падают.
bulgarian: Sales always go down during a heat wave.

english: I'm lucky Holt and Celine are willing to help with the store, great for all of our overheads!
french: J'ai beaucoup de chances quand Holt et Céline m'aident au magasin, ça réduit nos frais !
russian: Повезло, что Хольт и Селин помогают с магазином: это всем нам на пользу!
bulgarian: I'm lucky Holt and Celine are willing to help with the store, great for all of our overheads!

english: Holt's not so good with spicy food...
french: Holt n'apprécie pas beaucoup la nourriture épicée...
russian: Хольт не очень переносит острую еду...
bulgarian: Holt's not so good with spicy food...

english: Hope I'll see you at the General Store today, [Ari].
french: J'espère que tu passeras au magasin général aujourd'hui, [Ari].
russian: Надеюсь, заглянешь сегодня в лавку, [Ari].
bulgarian: Hope I'll see you at the General Store today, [Ari].

english: No one does dinner like the Sleeping Dragon!
french: Les dîners servis au Dragon qui dort sont délicieux !
russian: Никто не готовит так, как «Спящий дракон»!
bulgarian: No one does dinner like the Sleeping Dragon!

english: Hmm, the balances don't match... I wonder if Holt's having himself a snack from the shop's inventory again...
french: Mmm, j'ai des écarts entre ce que j'achète et ce que je vends... Je me demande si Holt n'aurait pas recommencé à se servir dans la réserve...
russian: Хм, учёт не сходится... интересно, это Хольт снова таскает вкусненькое из магазина?
bulgarian: Hmm, the balances don't match... I wonder if Holt's having himself a snack from the shop's inventory again...

english: You can leave your tesserae by the till! And if you need help with something, just flag one of us down.
french: Laisse tes tesserae à côté de la caisse ! Et si tu as besoin d'un renseignement, fais-nous signe.
russian: Можешь оставить тессеры у кассы! А если нужна помощь — просто позови кого-нибудь из нас.
bulgarian: You can leave your tesserae by the till! And if you need help with something, just flag one of us down.

english: The General Store is part of the lifeblood of Mistria. That's what gets me up in the morning.
french: Le magasin général est un pilier de notre ville. C'est ce qui me motive pour me lever le matin.
russian: Универмаг — часть сердца Мистрии. Именно эта мысль поднимает меня по утрам.
bulgarian: The General Store is part of the lifeblood of Mistria. That's what gets me up in the morning.

english: If these three ever want to start a band, I'd be first in line to be their manager!
french: Si ces trois-là décident de former un groupe, je serai la première à leur proposer mes services en tant qu'agent !
russian: Если эти трое решат собрать группу, я первая стану их менеджером!
bulgarian: If these three ever want to start a band, I'd be first in line to be their manager!

english: A good merchant looks at the world as a series of opportunities. That's good advice for a farmer too, [Ari]!
french: Un bon marchand voit le monde comme une série d'opportunités. Cela vaut aussi pour l'agriculture, [Ari] !
russian: Хороший торговец смотрит на мир как на череду возможностей. Земледельцу это тоже пригодится, [Ari]!
bulgarian: A good merchant looks at the world as a series of opportunities. That's good advice for a farmer too, [Ari]!

english: It's my day to mind the shop, [Ari]! Thanks for coming by, it's always nice to see a friendly face.
french: C'est à mon tour de tenir la boutique aujourd'hui, [Ari] ! Merci de ta visite, c'est toujours un plaisir de voir un visage souriant.
russian:
Сегодня моя очередь сидеть в магазине, [Ari]! Спасибо, что

заглянули

заглянулазаглянулзаглянуло. Всегда приятно видеть знакомое лицо.
bulgarian: It's my day to mind the shop, [Ari]! Thanks for coming by, it's always nice to see a friendly face.

english: Morning, [Ari]! Hope you're keeping busy on this fine day.
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! J'imagine que tu n'arrêtes pas par une si belle journée.
russian: Доброе утро, [Ari]! Надеюсь, дела у тебя идут хорошо в такой прекрасный день.
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! Hope you're keeping busy on this fine day.

english: Josephine's right! A morning bath is just the thing!
french: Joséphine a tout à fait raison ! Rien de tel qu'un bain de bon matin pour avoir de l'entrain !
russian: Джозефина права! Утренняя ванна — то, что нужно!
bulgarian: Josephine's right! A morning bath is just the thing!

english: Some morning shopping for you, [Ari]?
french: Tu es bien matinal<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they>, [Ari].
russian: Утренние покупки, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Some morning shopping for you, [Ari]?

english: Actually, Celine taught me how to make a salad. Hm.
french: En réalité, c'est Céline qui m'a appris comment faire. Hum.
russian: Хотя, на самом деле, это Селин меня научила. Хм.
bulgarian: Actually, Celine taught me how to make a salad. Hm.

english: I'm not quite the cook that Holt is, but I can make a fresh salad at least!
french: Je ne cuisine pas aussi bien que Holt, mais je sais au moins préparer une petite salade !
russian: Я не такой кулинар, как Хольт, но хоть свежий салат могу сделать!
bulgarian: I'm not quite the cook that Holt is, but I can make a fresh salad at least!

english: The numbers are looking good, Holt. It's an uptick from last month.
french: Par rapport au mois dernier, les chiffres sont bien meilleurs, Holt.
russian: Цифры радуют, Хольт. Рост по сравнению с прошлым месяцем.
bulgarian: The numbers are looking good, Holt. It's an uptick from last month.

english: I owe Josie some gossip... she always wants the latest on the Saturday Market.
french: J'ai quelques potins à raconter à Jo... Elle veut toujours tout savoir, quand vient le marché du samedi.
russian: Я задолжала Джози немного сплетен... она всегда хочет знать, что новенького на Субботнем базаре.
bulgarian: I owe Josie some gossip... she always wants the latest on the Saturday Market.

english: I hope Dell hasn't requisitioned it for the Dragonguard... again...
french: J'espère que Dell ne l'a pas encore « réquisitionné » pour la Garde des dragons...
russian: Надеюсь, Делл не забрала его для нужд Драконьей стражи... опять...
bulgarian: I hope Dell hasn't requisitioned it for the Dragonguard... again...

english: Now where did I put my pencil?
french: Où ai-je bien pu laisser traîner mon crayon ?
russian: Так... куда я положила карандаш?
bulgarian: Now where did I put my pencil?

english: The day after a Saturday Market always feels a bit slow by comparison.
french: Le dimanche après le marché, c'est toujours un peu calme.
russian: День после Субботнего базара всегда ощущается немного медленным.
bulgarian: The day after a Saturday Market always feels a bit slow by comparison.

english: The house looks extra cozy on rainy days...
french: Les jours de pluie, la maison paraît encore plus accueillante...
russian: В дождь дом кажется особенно уютным...
bulgarian: The house looks extra cozy on rainy days...

english: Unless I'm chasing Dell out of puddles.
french: À moins que je coure après Dell pour qu'elle ne saute pas dans les flaques.
russian: Если, конечно, не гоняю Делл из луж.
bulgarian: Unless I'm chasing Dell out of puddles.

english: Rain usually means it's slow at the General Store, so I take the day to run some errands.
french: Quand il pleut, c'est plutôt calme au magasin. J'en profite pour rattraper ce que je n'ai pas eu le temps de faire.
russian: В дождь в магазине обычно тихо, так что я занимаюсь делами по городу.
bulgarian: Rain usually means it's slow at the General Store, so I take the day to run some errands.

english: Everything's looking good for the Market tomorrow! Now I can enjoy Inn night without any worries.
french: Je crois que tout est prêt pour le marché de demain ! Je vais pouvoir me détendre à l'auberge, ce soir.
russian: Всё готово к завтрашнему базару! Можно спокойно наслаждаться вечером в трактире.
bulgarian: Everything's looking good for the Market tomorrow! Now I can enjoy Inn night without any worries.

english: Welcome, [Ari]! Have a look around and let me know if you have any questions.
french: Bienvenue, [Ari] ! Jette un œil et n'hésite pas si tu as la moindre question.
russian: Добро пожаловать, [Ari]! Оглянись как следует и дай знать, если будут вопросы.
bulgarian: Welcome, [Ari]! Have a look around and let me know if you have any questions.

english: Are you looking for Celine? She took a different shift this week.
french: Tu cherches Céline ? Elle n'a pas les mêmes horaires, cette semaine.
russian: Ищешь Селин? У неё на этой неделе другой график.
bulgarian: Are you looking for Celine? She took a different shift this week.

english: Take your time, I'm happy to help when you're ready.
french: Prends ton temps et dis-moi si je peux t'aider.
russian:
Не торопись, я помогу, когда будешь

готовы

готоваготовготово.
bulgarian: Take your time, I'm happy to help when you're ready.

english: We just restocked, [Ari]! Have a good look around.
french: Nous venons de nous réapprovisionner, [Ari] ! Vois si quelque chose te plaît.
russian: Мы только что пополнили запасы, [Ari]! Осмотрись хорошенько.
bulgarian: We just restocked, [Ari]! Have a good look around.

english: I just had an idea for the Saturday Market, but it'll have to wait till after my shift is over.
french: Je viens d'avoir une idée pour le marché, mais je vais devoir attendre la relève.
russian: Мне только что пришла идея для Субботнего базара, но придётся подождать до конца смены.
bulgarian: I just had an idea for the Saturday Market, but it'll have to wait till after my shift is over.

english: An organized shelf is a happy shelf!
french: Un rayon bien rangé attire les regards !
russian: Упорядоченная полка — счастливая полка!
bulgarian: An organized shelf is a happy shelf!

english: Balor's always bringing us produce you shipped! Thanks for your hard work, [Ari].
french: Balor n'arrête pas de nous apporter les produits que tu lui confies ! Merci de travailler si dur, [Ari].
russian: Балор всё время приносит нам урожай, который ты отправляешь! Спасибо за твою работу, [Ari].
bulgarian: Balor's always bringing us produce you shipped! Thanks for your hard work, [Ari].

english: "Omelet that slide."
french: « Même pas un petit bout de pain, ma mie ? »
russian: «Ну и оладно!»
bulgarian: "Omelet that slide."

english: Hahaha!
french: Ha ha ha !
russian: Ха-ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Hahaha!

english: Hahaha, [Ari]... my husband, I can't take it. I told him I was going to skip breakfast, and you know what he said?
french: Ha ha ha, [Ari]... Quel blagueur, mon mari ! Je lui ai dit que je comptais sauter le petit-déjeuner, et tu sais ce qu'il m'a répondu ?
russian: Ха-ха-ха, [Ari]... мой муж, я не могу с него. Я сказала, что пропущу завтрак, а он, знаешь, что ответил?
bulgarian: Hahaha, [Ari]... my husband, I can't take it. I told him I was going to skip breakfast, and you know what he said?

english: I think you could drive the economy of Mistria singlehandedly, [Ari]. I've never seen one person go through so much tesserae.
french: J'ai l'impression qu'à toi seul<he></he><she>e</she><they>·e</they>, tu pourrais faire tourner tout Mistria. Je n'ai jamais vu personne brasser autant de tesserae.
russian: Думаю, ты можешь в одиночку разогнать экономику Мистрии, [Ari]. Никогда не видела, чтобы один человек так активно тратил тессеры.
bulgarian: I think you could drive the economy of Mistria singlehandedly, [Ari]. I've never seen one person go through so much tesserae.

english: Oh, I do so love the look of a properly restocked shelf.
french: Oh, j'aime quand une étagère est bien remplie.
russian: О, как же я люблю вид аккуратно укомплектованной полки.
bulgarian: Oh, I do so love the look of a properly restocked shelf.

english: I'm still recovering from yesterday's Market Day, but I'm already planning for next week!
french: Je me remets encore du marché d'hier, mais je fais déjà des préparatifs pour la semaine prochaine !
russian: Я ещё не оправилась после вчерашнего базарного дня, а уже строю планы на следующий!
bulgarian: I'm still recovering from yesterday's Market Day, but I'm already planning for next week!

english: Sales go up when the sun's out.
french: Quand il fait beau, les ventes s'envolent.
russian: Когда светит солнце, продажи растут.
bulgarian: Sales go up when the sun's out.

english: A tidy store really puts my mind at ease.
french: Je ne me sens bien que quand je vois le magasin bien rangé.
russian: Чистый магазин сразу наводит порядок в голове.
bulgarian: A tidy store really puts my mind at ease.

english: Thanks for your patronage, [Ari]. Let me know if you need anything.
french: Merci de ta fidélité, [Ari]. Si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit, n'hésite pas.
russian: Спасибо за покупку, [Ari]. Дай знать, если что-нибудь понадобится.
bulgarian: Thanks for your patronage, [Ari]. Let me know if you need anything.

english: That's my girl!
french: Quelle chance j'ai d'avoir une fille comme elle !
russian: Вот это моя девочка!
bulgarian: That's my girl!

english: Oh, don't mind me, just tidying up while Celine is out. Can you believe she dusts the plants?
french: Oh, ne fais pas attention à moi. Je fais un brin de ménage pendant que Céline n'est pas là. Elle dépoussière même les plantes, tu le crois ça ?
russian: Не обращай внимания, я тут просто убираюсь, пока Селин нет. Представляешь, она пыль даже с растений вытирает!
bulgarian: Oh, don't mind me, just tidying up while Celine is out. Can you believe she dusts the plants?

english: Celine's very busy this week, so I thought I'd drop by and tidy up for her.
french: Céline a fort à faire cette semaine. Je me suis dit que j'allais passer faire un peu de rangement.
russian: У Селин на этой неделе много дел, так что я решила заглянуть и прибраться за неё.
bulgarian: Celine's very busy this week, so I thought I'd drop by and tidy up for her.

english: Maybe I'll just tidy up a little bit.
french: Je vais peut-être faire un peu de ménage.
russian: Наверное, просто немного приберусь.
bulgarian: Maybe I'll just tidy up a little bit.

english: Oh hey, [Ari]! I thought I'd check on Celine, but she's not here.
french: Tiens, bonjour [Ari] ! Je venais voir Céline, mais elle n'est pas là.
russian: О, привет, [Ari]! Я хотела навестить Селин, но её нет.
bulgarian: Oh hey, [Ari]! I thought I'd check on Celine, but she's not here.

english: I thought I'd come by and tidy up, but she keeps the place pretty clean! That's my girl.
french: Je pensais faire un petit peu de ménage, mais c'est déjà impeccable. Ma fille est merveilleuse !
russian: Я пришла немного прибраться, но у неё и так всё чисто! Вот это моя девочка.
bulgarian: I thought I'd come by and tidy up, but she keeps the place pretty clean! That's my girl.

english: Oh, were you looking for Celine? She's out.
french: Oh, tu viens voir Céline ? Elle n'est pas là.
russian: Ты Селин ищешь? Её нет.
bulgarian: Oh, were you looking for Celine? She's out.

english: Celine keeps her place pretty clean! I don't know if I need to be tidying up for her anymore.
french: Céline aime que sa maison soit propre ! Je ne sais pas si ça vaut encore la peine que je passe lui faire du ménage.
russian: Селин хорошо убирается! Похоже, мне уже и не нужно ей помогать.
bulgarian: Celine keeps her place pretty clean! I don't know if I need to be tidying up for her anymore.

english: That Balor is tight-lipped about his suppliers, but I'll crack him yet.
french: Ce Balor... Il ne veut pas dire où il se fournit, mais j'arriverai à le faire parler.
russian: Балор не хочет раскрывать, откуда он берёт товары, но я его рано или поздно раскручу.
bulgarian: That Balor is tight-lipped about his suppliers, but I'll crack him yet.

english: I can ring you up whenever you're ready.
french: Je suis prête à t'encaisser dès que tu auras terminé.
russian:
Я тебя рассчитаю, как только будешь

готоваготовготово.
bulgarian: I can ring you up whenever you're ready.

english: You know you've had too much wine when you're not the least bit hungry by the time dinner rolls around...
french: Si tu n'as pas faim à l'heure du dîner, c'est en général que tu as un peu forcé sur le vin...
russian: Понимаешь, что перебрала с вином, когда к ужину уже совсем не хочется есть...
bulgarian: You know you've had too much wine when you're not the least bit hungry by the time dinner rolls around...

english: Jo sent me home with some stew... Reina prepared the potatoes for this, you can tell by the the blend of spices!
french: Jo m'a donné du ragoût à rapporter à la maison... C'est Reina qui a cuisiné les patates. Ça se sent aux épices qu'elle a utilisées !
russian: Джо отдала мне немного рагу с собой... Картошку готовила Рейна, это видно по специям!
bulgarian: Jo sent me home with some stew... Reina prepared the potatoes for this, you can tell by the the blend of spices!

english: After the earthquake, we had to redraw all the trade routes. We're still redrawing them, in fact.
french: Après le tremblement de terre, il a fallu repenser toutes les routes commerciales. D'ailleurs, ce n'est pas tout à fait terminé.
russian: После землетрясения нам пришлось перечерчивать все торговые маршруты. Мы до сих пор этим занимаемся.
bulgarian: After the earthquake, we had to redraw all the trade routes. We're still redrawing them, in fact.

english: I've got a work date with Adeline.
french: J'ai une séance de travail avec Adeline.
russian: У меня сегодня рабочая встреча с Аделиной.
bulgarian: I've got a work date with Adeline.

english: It's nice to unwind with some friends, isn't it?
french: Quel plaisir de se détendre entre amis, n'est-ce pas ?
russian: Приятно просто посидеть с друзьями, правда?
bulgarian: It's nice to unwind with some friends, isn't it?

english: Holt must be on his way over...
french: Holt ne devrait pas tarder...
russian: Похоже, Хольт уже в пути...
bulgarian: Holt must be on his way over...

english: It's not so dire that anyone's at risk of going hungry...
french: Personne ne risque encore d'avoir la faim au ventre, ce n'est pas à ce point...
russian: Всё не настолько плохо. Пока никто не рискует остаться без еды...
bulgarian: It's not so dire that anyone's at risk of going hungry...

english: But I'm really looking forward to some big produce shipments from $[farm_name]$.
french: Mais j'ai vraiment hâte de recevoir de grosses livraisons de produits cultivés à $[farm_name]$ !
russian: Но я очень жду больших поставок продуктов с фермы $«[farm_name]»$.
bulgarian: But I'm really looking forward to some big produce shipments from $[farm_name]$.

english: And the sooner, the better!
french: Et le plus tôt sera le mieux !
russian: И чем скорее, тем лучше!
bulgarian: And the sooner, the better!

english: We're getting low on some essentials at the store, but we'll just have to make do until our next supply shipment comes in.
french: Nos réserves de produits de base baissent, au magasin, mais il faudra faire avec jusqu'à ce que nous soyons réapprovisionnés.
russian: В магазине заканчиваются некоторые товары первой необходимости, но придётся потерпеть до следующей поставки.
bulgarian: We're getting low on some essentials at the store, but we'll just have to make do until our next supply shipment comes in.

english: The latest delivery we received from Balor wasn't the price we were expecting...
french: La dernière livraison que nous avons reçue de Balor ne nous a pas coûté ce qu'on pensait...
russian: Цена на последнюю поставку от Балора была не такая, как мы ожидали...
bulgarian: The latest delivery we received from Balor wasn't the price we were expecting...

english: Somehow, it was lower.
french: Bizarrement, c'était moins cher.
russian: Почему-то она оказалась ниже.
bulgarian: Somehow, it was lower.

english: How is that possible? In this market?
french: Comment est-ce possible ? Vu les prix du marché ?
russian: Как у него это вышло? При таких рыночных условиях!
bulgarian: How is that possible? In this market?

english: You don't think...
french: Il n'aurait quand même pas...
russian: Как думаешь, может быть, он...
bulgarian: You don't think...

english: No. Nevermind.
french: Non. Rien.
russian: Хотя нет. Не важно.
bulgarian: No. Nevermind.

english: Strange...
french: C'est étrange...
russian: Странно...
bulgarian: Strange...

english: Since you're just down the road, maybe you could stop in and say hello now and then.
french: Comme elle habite juste à côté de chez toi, tu pourrais peut-être passer lui dire bonjour de temps en temps ?
russian: Можешь иногда заходить к ней проверить, как у неё дела? Тебе же там недалеко.
bulgarian: Since you're just down the road, maybe you could stop in and say hello now and then.

english: What can I say? A mother worries.
french: Que veux-tu...? Une maman s'inquiète toujours pour sa fille.
russian: Что поделать? Как мать я волнуюсь.
bulgarian: What can I say? A mother worries.

english: Celine only recently moved out to her own place...
french: Céline vient tout juste de prendre son indépendance...
russian: Селин совсем недавно съехала от нас в свой домик...
bulgarian: Celine only recently moved out to her own place...

english: Ryis helped us patch it up again, but there's no denying the store's going to need some bigger repairs before long.
french: Ryis nous a aidés à le rafistoler de nouveau, mais il faut se rendre à l'évidence, le magasin va avoir de besoin de grosses réparations sous peu.
russian: Риз снова помог нам её залатать, но не поспоришь: скоро магазину понадобится ремонт посерьёзнее.
bulgarian: Ryis helped us patch it up again, but there's no denying the store's going to need some bigger repairs before long.

english: Ugh... I can't believe the roof sprung another leak...
french: Pfff... On a eu une nouvelle fuite sur le toit...
russian: Уф... Не верится, что крыша снова протекла...
bulgarian: Ugh... I can't believe the roof sprung another leak...

english: The shop's a little quieter on the weekends.
french: C'est toujours un peu plus calme au magasin le week-end.
russian: В выходные в магазине чуть тише.
bulgarian: The shop's a little quieter on the weekends.

english: Good afternoon! Feel free to browse, everything is fresh and local!
french: Bonjour ! Vois si quelque chose te tente, tout est frais et local.
russian: Добрый день! Осмотрись, всё свежее и местного производства!
bulgarian: Good afternoon! Feel free to browse, everything is fresh and local!

english: Our winter inventory is going well! I'm so pleased.
french: Nos produits d'hiver se vendent très bien ! Je suis ravie.
russian: Зимние запасы идут отлично! Я так рада.
bulgarian: Our winter inventory is going well! I'm so pleased.

english: Goodness, look at this! How many hands do you think this =Ancient Gold Coin= passed through? It's beautiful, thank you.
french: Bon sang, regarde ça ! Tu imagines par combien de mains cette =pièce d'or antique= a pu passer. Elle est magnifique, merci.
russian: Боже, только посмотри! Через сколько же рук прошла эта =древняя золотая монета=? Она прекрасна, спасибо.
bulgarian: Goodness, look at this! How many hands do you think this =Ancient Gold Coin= passed through? It's beautiful, thank you.

english: Holt is always leaving me presents, so I didn't put it together. Thank you, [Ari]!
french: Holt m'offre toujours des tas de choses, alors je n'avais pas réalisé. Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Хольт всё время дарит мне подарки, так что я и не связала. Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Holt is always leaving me presents, so I didn't put it together. Thank you, [Ari]!

english: For me? Oh goodness, it's my birthday, isn't it?
french: C'est pour moi ? Oh, c'est mon anniversaire, c'est ça ?
russian: Для меня? Ах да, сегодня же мой день рождения, да?
bulgarian: For me? Oh goodness, it's my birthday, isn't it?

english: =Coffee=! This is going to power me through my paperwork. Thank you, [Ari].
french: Un =café= ! Voilà qui va me donner de l'énergie pour m'occuper de ma paperasse. Merci, [Ari].
russian: =Кофе=! Он поможет мне разобраться с бумагами. Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: =Coffee=! This is going to power me through my paperwork. Thank you, [Ari].

english: Hm, I'm not even sure I could sell this.
french: Mmm, je ne crois pas que j'arriverai à vendre ça.
russian: Хм, я не уверена, что смогу это хотя бы продать.
bulgarian: Hm, I'm not even sure I could sell this.

english: Thanks [Ari], I like this a lot.
french: Merci, [Ari]. Ça me plaît beaucoup.
russian: Спасибо, [Ari], мне это очень по вкусу.
bulgarian: Thanks [Ari], I like this a lot.

english: Looks delicious! Thanks for thinking of me, [Ari].
french: Ça a l'air délicieux ! Merci d'avoir pensé à moi, [Ari].
russian: Выглядит вкусно! Спасибо, что думаешь обо мне, [Ari].
bulgarian: Looks delicious! Thanks for thinking of me, [Ari].

english: Thank you, [Ari]! I love it.
french: Merci infiniment, [Ari] ! C'est tout ce que j'aime.
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]! Мне очень нравится.
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari]! I love it.

english: You're so thoughtful, [Ari]! It's not often I receive something and want to keep it all to myself.
french: Quelle délicate attention, [Ari] ! C'est rare qu'on m'offre quelque chose que j'aie envie de garder pour moi.
russian:
Ты

такие внимательные

такая внимательнаятакой внимательныйтакое внимательное, [Ari]! Редко получаешь что-то, что хочется оставить целиком себе.

english: Did Holt tell you this is one of my favorites? Thank you [Ari], I'm going to savor this!
french: C'est Holt qui t'a dit que j'adorais ça ? Merci, [Ari]. Je vais me régaler.
russian: Это Хольт рассказал тебе, что я это люблю? Спасибо, [Ari], я буду смаковать!
bulgarian: Did Holt tell you this is one of my favorites? Thank you [Ari], I'm going to savor this!

english: [Ari], what am I supposed to do with moss?
french: [Ari], tu m'expliques ce que je suis censée faire de cette mousse ?
russian: [Ari], и что мне делать с мхом?
bulgarian: [Ari], what am I supposed to do with moss?

english: Ah, thank you.
french: Ah, merci.
russian: Ах, спасибо.
bulgarian: Ah, thank you.

english: Dell may tell you otherwise, but she is NOT allowed to have any coffee. Not after... #The Incident.#
french: Même si elle te dit le contraire, sache que Dell n'a absolument PAS le droit de boire du café. Pas après... #l'incident#.
russian: Делл может говорить что угодно, но кофе ей НЕЛЬЗЯ. Не после... #того случая.#
bulgarian: Dell may tell you otherwise, but she is NOT allowed to have any coffee. Not after... #The Incident.#

english: I've been in talks with Darcy to get some of her coffee beans at the General Store! We'll see if it works out.
french: Je suis en pourparlers avec Darcy pour vendre son café dans notre magasin ! J'espère que ça aboutira.
russian: Я веду переговоры с Дарси, чтобы продавать её кофе в универмаге! Посмотрим, что из этого выйдет.
bulgarian: I've been in talks with Darcy to get some of her coffee beans at the General Store! We'll see if it works out.

english: Darcy's got a good head for business... I like that.
french: Darcy est dure en affaires... et ça n'est pas pour me déplaire.
russian: У Дарси хорошая деловая хватка... мне это нравится.
bulgarian: Darcy's got a good head for business... I like that.

english: I really look forward to a =Latte= at Darcy's... it helps shake off some of the week's fatigue.
french: J'ai hâte d'aller déguster un =café latte= chez Darcy... Ça me permet d'évacuer un peu la fatigue de la semaine.
russian: Я правда с нетерпением жду, когда смогу выпить =латте= у Дарси... Это помогает снять недельную усталость.
bulgarian: I really look forward to a =Latte= at Darcy's... it helps shake off some of the week's fatigue.

english: Valen was right, Louis does make a nice pair of slacks!
french: Valen a raison. Les pantalons confectionnés par Louis sont de très bonne qualité !
russian: Вален была права, Луи и правда шьёт отличные брюки!
bulgarian: Valen was right, Louis does make a nice pair of slacks!

english: Dell, on the other hand, just wants overalls in every color of the rainbow.
french: Quant à Dell, elle ne met que des salopettes, mais elle en veut de toutes les couleurs possibles et imaginables !
russian: А Делл, наоборот, хочет комбинезоны всех цветов радуги.
bulgarian: Dell, on the other hand, just wants overalls in every color of the rainbow.

english: I was so relieved when Celine started choosing her own clothes, she was so picky!
french: J'ai été tellement soulagée quand Céline s'est mise à choisir seule ses vêtements. Elle était si difficile !
russian: Я вздохнула с таким облегчением, когда Селин сама стала выбирать одежду: она такая привередливая!
bulgarian: I was so relieved when Celine started choosing her own clothes, she was so picky!

english: I don't really need new clothes right now, but this blazer does look nice...
french: Je n'ai pas vraiment besoin de nouveaux vêtements, mais je dois avouer que cette veste est tentante...
russian: Сейчас мне не особо нужны новые вещи, но этот пиджак выглядит симпатично...
bulgarian: I don't really need new clothes right now, but this blazer does look nice...

english: Louis understands my taste in clothing... professional without sacrificing comfort!
french: Louis connaît parfaitement mes goûts. Mes tenues doivent être sérieuses mais confortables.
russian: Луи понимает мой вкус: деловой стиль без ущерба для комфорта!
bulgarian: Louis understands my taste in clothing... professional without sacrificing comfort!

english: Merri's booth was a bit of a logistical nightmare until Hayden and Olric volunteered to help her shift her furniture. Those boys love to pick up anything and everything.
french: Le stand de Merri ressemblait à un bazar, puis Olric et Hayden se sont proposés pour réorganiser l'agencement des meubles. Ces garçons n'hésitent pas à se mettre au service des autres.
russian: Лавка Мэрри была сущим кошмаром для логистики, пока Хейден и Ольрик не вызвались помочь ей двигать мебель. Эти парни любят всё перетаскивать.
bulgarian: Merri's booth was a bit of a logistical nightmare until Hayden and Olric volunteered to help her shift her furniture. Those boys love to pick up anything and everything.

english: Merri always brings such nice pieces to the market. We're lucky to have her!
french: Merri a toujours des meubles intéressants à vendre. Sa présence est une aubaine !
russian: Мэрри всегда привозит на базар такие классные вещи. Нам с ней повезло!
bulgarian: Merri always brings such nice pieces to the market. We're lucky to have her!

english: Merri's got some handsome bookshelves for sale... I do need an easy place to store all our accounting...
french: Merri a de très belles étagères à vendre... et j'aurais bien besoin d'un endroit pour ranger ma compta...
russian: У Мэрри есть симпатичные книжные полки... мне бы не помешало удобное место для всей бухгалтерии...
bulgarian: Merri's got some handsome bookshelves for sale... I do need an easy place to store all our accounting...

english: Our produce display at the General Store came from Merri's... they're almost a hundred seasons old, but Merri restored them good as new!
french: Les présentoirs du magasin général viennent de chez Merri... Ils étaient très anciens, mais elle les a restaurés à merveille !
russian: Наш овощной прилавок в универмаге — тоже от Мэрри... ему уже почти сто сезонов, а она отреставрировала так, что он как новенький!
bulgarian: Our produce display at the General Store came from Merri's... they're almost a hundred seasons old, but Merri restored them good as new!

english: When Stillwell approached me about running a booth, I wasn't too sure... but he's become a cornerstone of the Saturday Market. A dark, dreary cornerstone...
bulgarian: When Stillwell approached me about running a booth, I wasn't too sure... but he's become a cornerstone of the Saturday Market. A dark, dreary cornerstone...

english: "Oh foolish fool, who asks after the most foolish of things..." I asked Stillwell for a money fortune, not his opinion... I suppose he can't help himself.
bulgarian: "Oh foolish fool, who asks after the most foolish of things..." I asked Stillwell for a money fortune, not his opinion... I suppose he can't help himself.

english: Celine loves getting her fortune from Stillwell, but Dell refuses... those sisters do go their own way.
bulgarian: Celine loves getting her fortune from Stillwell, but Dell refuses... those sisters do go their own way.

english: You know, I'm beginning to think that Stillwell's gloomy delivery is part of his marketing.
bulgarian: You know, I'm beginning to think that Stillwell's gloomy delivery is part of his marketing.

english: After all his talk of Mistria as a backwater... you just know he sees the potential of the folks here.
french: Vu qu'il a qualifié Mistria de trou perdu... on sait comment il considère les gens d'ici.
russian: После того, как он обозвал Мистрию захолустьем... Всё же он явно видит в местных жителях потенциал.
bulgarian: After all his talk of Mistria as a backwater... you just know he sees the potential of the folks here.

english: Taliferro... now there's someone who surprised me when they signed up for the Saturday Market.
french: Taliferro... On peut dire que j'ai été surprise de le voir s'inscrire au marché du samedi.
russian: Талиферро... Вот от него я не ожидала участия в Субботнем базаре.
bulgarian: Taliferro... now there's someone who surprised me when they signed up for the Saturday Market.

english: Well, not formal ones, anyway.
french: Pas officiellement, en tout cas.
russian: Во всяком случае, не формальные.
bulgarian: Well, not formal ones, anyway.

english: I wouldn't say I've received complaints about Taliferro, exactly...
french: Je dois reconnaître que personne ne s'est plaint de Taliferro...
russian: Не могу прямо сказать, что мне приходили жалобы на Талиферро...
bulgarian: I wouldn't say I've received complaints about Taliferro, exactly...

english: Or maybe it's the opportunity for food puns?
french: Ou alors, c'est juste pour placer ses jeux de mots ?
russian: Или для него это просто возможность пошутить каламбуры про еду?
bulgarian: Or maybe it's the opportunity for food puns?

english: Holt really gets fired up over Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$...
french: Holt est obnubilé par le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro...
russian: Хольт так загорается каждый раз, когда Талиферро объявляет $смотр блюд$...
bulgarian: Holt really gets fired up over Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$...

english: And told her to add extra mud!
french: Et je lui ai dit de ne pas lésiner sur la boue !
russian: И попросила класть побольше грязи!
bulgarian: And told her to add extra mud!

english: When I heard Dell was submitting mud pies to Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$, I marched right over...
french: En apprenant que Dell allait préparer une tarte à la boue pour le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro, je suis allée la voir...
russian: Когда я узнала, что Делл приносит Талиферро на $смотр блюд$ пирожки с грязью, я сразу пришла к ней...
bulgarian: When I heard Dell was submitting mud pies to Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$, I marched right over...

english: I used to dye my hair myself... Thankfully, Vera does a much better job.
french: Avant, je me teignais moi-même les cheveux... Fort heureusement, Vera le fait beaucoup mieux que moi.
russian: Раньше я сама красила себе волосы... Хорошо, что теперь это делает Вера: у неё получается куда лучше.
bulgarian: I used to dye my hair myself... Thankfully, Vera does a much better job.

english: Dell really wants to dye her hair blue... but could she sit still for long enough?
french: Dell a très envie de se faire teindre les cheveux en bleu... mais je ne suis pas sûre qu'elle tiendra en place assez longtemps.
russian: Делл очень хочет покраситься в синий... но сможет ли она усидеть на месте достаточно долго?
bulgarian: Dell really wants to dye her hair blue... but could she sit still for long enough?

english: When I told Celine I used to dye my hair blue, she looked like she didn't believe me... maybe I should surprise her.
french: Quand j'ai dit à Céline que je voulais me faire teindre en bleu, je crois qu'elle ne m'a pas prise au sérieux... Je devrais peut-être la surprendre.
russian: Когда я сказала Селин, что раньше красила волосы в синий, она посмотрела на меня, будто не поверила... может, стоит её удивить.
bulgarian: When I told Celine I used to dye my hair blue, she looked like she didn't believe me... maybe I should surprise her.

english: I'm so glad to have Vera back at the market. Holt and Dell can never sit still when I try to give them a trim.
french: Je suis si contente que Vera soit revenue au marché. Holt et Dell bougent trop pour que je puisse leur couper les cheveux.
russian: Я так рада, что Вера снова на базаре. Хольт и Делл никогда не сидят спокойно, когда я пытаюсь их подстричь.
bulgarian: I'm so glad to have Vera back at the market. Holt and Dell can never sit still when I try to give them a trim.

english: Why would we pay an additional 3000t after footing the bill for this booth?
french: Pourquoi on lui donnerait 3 000 tesserae alors qu'on a déjà payé son stand ?
russian: С чего бы нам платить ещё 3000 сверху, когда мы уже оплатили его лавку?
bulgarian: Why would we pay an additional 3000t after footing the bill for this booth?

english: Wheedle showed up to the Saturday Market, and then tried to extract an appearance fee! Of 3000t!
french: Wheedle a débarqué au marché du samedi et il a voulu que je lui paie un cachet ! Un cachet de 3 000 tesserae !
russian: Хлюст пришёл на Субботний базар и запросил гонорар за участие! 3000 тессер!
bulgarian: Wheedle showed up to the Saturday Market, and then tried to extract an appearance fee! Of 3000t!

english: That's a public bridge! It's for everyone!
french: C'est un bien public ! Il est à tout le monde !
russian: Это же общий мост! Он для всех там стоит!
bulgarian: That's a public bridge! It's for everyone!

english: You know, I once caught Wheedle trying to sell Olric that bridge on the east side of town?
french: Tu sais, un jour, j'ai surpris Wheedle en train d'essayer de vendre le pont à l'est de la ville à Olric.
russian: Знаешь, я однажды застала Хлюста за попыткой продаль Ольрику мост к востоку от города.
bulgarian: You know, I once caught Wheedle trying to sell Olric that bridge on the east side of town?

english: I think he was trying to establish a monopoly.
french: Je crois qu'il voulait avoir le monopole.
russian: Я думаю, он пытался установить монополию.
bulgarian: I think he was trying to establish a monopoly.

english: Wheedle tried to buy out the rest of the booths at the Saturday Market, so he'd be the only one running a stall.
french: Wheedle a essayé de racheter tous les stands du marché du samedi pour pouvoir être le seul à s'installer.
russian: Хлюст хотел выкупить все остальные лавки на Субботнем базаре, чтобы остаться единственным продавцом.
bulgarian: Wheedle tried to buy out the rest of the booths at the Saturday Market, so he'd be the only one running a stall.

english: Just one!
french: Une seule !
russian: Ну хоть один!
bulgarian: Just one!

english: I'd like to get through one Saturday Market without Wheedle stirring up some kind of trouble.
french: J'aimerais tellement que, juste une fois, Wheedle ne fasse pas des siennes au marché du samedi.
russian: Хотела бы я хоть один Субботний базар пережить без неприятностей от Хлюста.
bulgarian: I'd like to get through one Saturday Market without Wheedle stirring up some kind of trouble.

english: She seemed really interested to give it a try!
french: Elle a eu l'air très intéressée et prête à essayer !
russian: Она сказала: интересно попробовать!
bulgarian: She seemed really interested to give it a try!

english: I asked Zorel what she thought about a new kind of music, for when people do their grocery shopping.
french: J'ai demandé à Zorel ce qu'elle pensait d'un possible nouveau genre de musique, pour quand les gens font leurs courses.
russian: Я спросила Зорель, как ей идея делать специальную музыку, чтобы включать на фоне, когда люди ходят за покупками.
bulgarian: I asked Zorel what she thought about a new kind of music, for when people do their grocery shopping.

english: A coin that grand is worthy of putting on display.
french: Ce genre de pièce mérite d'être exposée.
russian: Такую монету и правда стоило выставить напоказ.
bulgarian: A coin that grand is worthy of putting on display.

english: I'm partial to tesserae, but the =Ancient Gold Coin= on view at the Museum is a pretty bit of currency.
french: J'ai un faible pour les tesserae, mais la =pièce d'or antique= du musée est vraiment du plus bel effet.
russian: Мне по душе и обычные тессеры, но та =древняя золотая монета=, выставленная в музее, — вещица красивая.
bulgarian: I'm partial to tesserae, but the =Ancient Gold Coin= on view at the Museum is a pretty bit of currency.

english: Ancient economies often had unique ways of looking at money.
french: Les anciennes sociétés avaient souvent des façons bien différentes de voir l'argent.
russian: В древние времена к деньгам часто относились весьма необычно.
bulgarian: Ancient economies often had unique ways of looking at money.

english: There's a $Coin Lump$ over at the Museum! I wonder if Errol would let me take a closer look some time.
french: Tu as vu cet $amas de pièces$ au musée ! Je me demande si Errol m'autoriserait à le regarder de plus près, un de ces jours...
russian: В музее есть $комок монет$! Интересно, Эррол даст мне рассмотреть его поближе?
bulgarian: There's a $Coin Lump$ over at the Museum! I wonder if Errol would let me take a closer look some time.
